issues.description: The template's Stock.findStockIngredient method signature requires a boolean caseSensitive parameter, but the problem statement UML and the solution use a single-parameter signature findStockIngredient(String). Additionally, other methods in the template (add, take) and the Main test code call findStockIngredient with a single String argument. This parameter mismatch in the template will cause compilation errors and prevents students from following the specified design.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template Stock.findStockIngredient signature match the specification and solution by providing a single-parameter method: public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name). Update its implementation accordingly (e.g., use equals or equalsIgnoreCase as intended). Alternatively, provide an overloaded method findStockIngredient(String name) that delegates to the two-parameter variant to preserve any case-sensitive behavior.

issues.description: The problem specification and solution expect a Stock.findStockIngredient(String) method (single-string parameter), but the template Stock class exposes findStockIngredient(String, boolean) (an extra caseSensitive boolean parameter). This mismatch in the method signature (same conceptual operation but different identifier/parameterization) can confuse students when mapping the UML / problem text to the provided template code and when invoking the method (the rest of template code and examples call the single-parameter form).
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method signature across artifacts: provide Stock.findStockIngredient(String name) as declared in the problem and implemented in the solution. If case-sensitive behavior is required, either implement an overload findStockIngredient(String, boolean) delegating to the single-argument method or add an optional/explicit parameter name but keep the single-argument form available so examples and UML map directly to the template.
